Phase 2.6 — Folder-backup encryption rewrite is now locked against regression: `electron/services/chatFolderBackupService.ts` ships a libsodium Argon2id13 + XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF envelope with fresh per-backup DEK, KEK derived from the user-supplied passphrase, structured `BackupStructureError` preservation, and IPC-side `isExportFolderBackupInput` / `isImportFolderBackupInput` validators. The v2 wire format guarantees no cleartext manifest, no `keyWrapped` field, no passphrase leak, and no `metadata.ciphertext` legacy path. Eight targeted tests in `electron/services/chatFolderBackupService.test.ts` cover wire-format enforcement, passphrase gates, AEAD tag mismatch, and v1 backup rejection; the full Electron test segment (724/724) and the full `npm run ci` parity commands (`lint:eslint`, `typecheck` Electron, `verify:safety-guard`, `verify:markdown-links`, `verify:contracts`, `build`, `verify:dist`) all run green. This closes the documented Phase 2.6 implementation; remaining Phase 2 sub-work (folder lock / unlock state, standard vs character folder separation infrastructure) is tracked under the parent `vo-phase-2` todo row and outside Phase 2.6 scope.

**Phase 2.x renderer closeout (2026-07-20 continuation):** the remaining Phase 2 gap was the renderer surface — `src/stores/chat-folder-store.ts` previously exposed only 6 of the 14 expected operations (load/create/rename/reorder/move/delete). This session extended `ChatFolderState` and the Zustand store with the missing 7 — `getBackupPreview`, `exportFolderBackup`, `previewImport`, `importFolderBackup`, `lockFolder`, `unlockFolder`, `getFolderLockState` — each routing through the existing `desktopBridge.desktopChatFolders` IPC chain so Phase 2.5 lock backoff and Phase 2.6 libsodium backup become addressable from the renderer. Lock/unlock intentionally returns the structured `{ ok, error, retryAfter? }` response without forcing a success toast on failure (the renderer renders the backoff dialog); backup operators toast on success and reuse the existing failure toast text. `vo-phase-2` is now closed in the Open TODO Ledger.

**vo-shared closeout (2026-07-20 continuation 5 — Phase 6 Shared type / IPC contract parity):** closed `vo-shared` by adding the canonical shared contract `src/shared/chatMediaReferenceContracts.ts` (`ChatMediaType`, `ChatMediaOperation`, `CHAT_MEDIA_TYPES`, `CHAT_MEDIA_OPERATIONS`, `CHAT_MEDIA_REF_ID_RE`, `MAX_CHAT_MEDIA_REF_FIELDS = 11`, `ChatMediaReferenceContract`, `CreateChatMediaReferenceInputContract`, `isChatMediaReferenceContract`, `isChatMediaReferenceArrayContract`) and the parity regression guard `src/shared/chatMediaReferenceContracts.test.ts` (9 cases / 9 PASS). The contract uses millisecond-epoch `createdAt`/`deletedFromChatAt` to match `src/types/conversationVault.ts:60` (initial ISO-string mis-typing caught on the first typecheck and corrected before the green run). A `fieldCount > 11` cap prevents corrupt serialized rows from inflating validation costs; an array cap of length 512 protects `coerce` consumers from runaway payloads. Tombstone (`deletedFromChatAt: number`) and orphan (`orphanedFromChat: true`) shapes both pass the contract — proving the tombstone filter belongs in chat-store / message-bubble layers, not the shared shape validator. A string-shaped `deletedFromChatAt` is correctly rejected as schema drift. The shared predicates are an additive public API; chat-store and media-store can adopt them at their own pace. Combined regression: `src/shared/chatMediaReferenceContracts.test.ts + src/stores/chat-media-reference.test.ts + src/stores/media-store.test.ts + src/stores/chat-store.web.test.ts` → **87/87 PASS across 4 files**; `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` zero-error. - **P0-03 — Agent runner emitted non-canonical `{mediaId, mimeType}` stub on generated MediaMessages (`electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.ts`):** deleted the legacy `metadata.generatedMedia = { mediaId, mimeType }` block and added the module-level `extractCanonicalChatMediaReferences(toolResult)` helper. The helper validates `data.chatRef` against `isChatMediaReferenceArrayContract` (from `src/shared/chatMediaReferenceContracts.ts`) and emits `metadata.generatedMedia = [ref]` only when refs length > 0. The downstream `upsertGeneratedMedia` path at `src/stores/chat-store.ts:601-672` now consumes a properly-typed record. Regression: `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.test.ts` (4 cases / 4 PASS) — covers valid ref → 1-entry array, multiple refs → array in order, empty `data.chatRef` → undefined, legacy stub → undefined.
- **P0-04 — `executeMediaTool` issued raw `fetch()` against api.venice.ai (`electron/agent/runtime/agent-tool-executor.ts`):** replaced the raw `fetch('https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/image/generate', {…})` body with a call to `performGuardedVeniceRequest({endpoint:"/image/generate", method:"POST", body, profileId, agentSessionId})` from `electron/services/guardPipeline.ts:170`. Local Family Safe Mode preflight, runtime `safe_mode` override, response screening, retries with backoff, abort propagation, idempotency (`conversation_id`/prompt hash), and traffic inspector logging now all run as part of the rendezvous. Other `media.*` tools fail closed via `CAPABILITY_DENIED`. The executor returns a canonical `data.chatRef` (id, mediaId, mediaType, operation, displayUrl, thumbnailUrl, altText, modelId, createdAt, mimeType) rather than `{url, hash, mimeType, source}` legacy stub. Regression: `electron/agent/runtime/agent-tool-executor.test.ts` (7 cases / 7 PASS) — covers happy-path POST + chatRef shape, 451 block returns `data.error` not `data.chatRef`, 401/403 surfaces upstream error, model `safe_mode` honours toggled dispatcher, request forwarding carries `profileId`/`agentSessionId`, `media.upscale` returns `CAPABILITY_DENIED`, abort mid-flight cancels via `AbortController`.
- **P0-05 — `composeTrustedRequest` discarded the tool runtime layer + chat-only injection (`electron/agent/runtime/trusted-agent-request.ts`):** trust runtime correctness overhaul.
  - `TRUSTED_PRIORITY_FLOOR = 0` + immutable-floor guard: `composeAgentRuntime` rejects any customLayer with `priority < 0` once the trusted layer is registered ("custom layer 'X' priority -1 violates immutable priority floor 0").
  - `fnv1a64(str)` BigInt FNV-64 + `dedupToolRuntimeLayers(layers)` — collapses identical tool-runtime layers via a content fingerprint (sorted `[name]=trusted` joined with `|`) so identical registries collapse to a single runtime layer. Trust-runtime module is free of Node-only `crypto.createHash`.
  - `composeTrustedRequest` no longer does `void buildToolRuntimeLayer(tools)`: the layer is now attached to every POST. Tool names extracted from `{type:"function", function:{name}}` records (`isRecord` narrowing; `typeof fn.name === 'string'` assertion) and fallback plain-string shapes.
  - Universal-POST injection: chat prepends the trusted block to `messages[0].content`; non-chat POSTs (`/image/generate`, `/image/upscale`, `/image/edit`, `/image/multi-edit`, `/augment/text-parser`, `/audio/queue`, `/audio/speech`, `/audio/transcriptions`, `/embeddings`, `/video/queue`, `/video/quote`, `/video/complete`) prepend `[System Runtime Context]` to `body.prompt`. Non-POST requests (GETs) and non-allowed methods return the body unchanged.
  - New exported `substituteTimeAndDatePlaceholders(systemPrompt, layer)` — runs `{{time && date}}` / `{{date}}` / `{{time}}` / `{{timezone}}` / `{{iso}}` substitution inside the compose step so user-authored templates are deterministic across chat-completions and image/audio/etc endpoints.
  - Regression: `electron/agent/runtime/trusted-agent-request.test.ts` (10 cases — 4 original + 6 P0-XX) / 10 PASS — covers `composeAgentRuntime accepts non-trusted layers above priority floor`, `composeAgentRuntime rejects non-trusted layers below priority floor`, `dedup of identical tool-runtime layers by content hash (3 distinct tool-runtime layers survive: alpha, alpha|beta, gamma)`, `composeTrustedRequest attaches tool layer to chat-completions and prefixes messages[0]`, `composeTrustedRequest attaches tool layer to image-generate and prefixes body.prompt`, `{{time && date}} substitution`.
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md:7`** appended `> Reopened for P0 remediation — 2026-07-20 session` blockquote listing P0-01..P0-05 with file paths, regression test files, and assertion counts (original 9-phase closure narrative preserved intact).

**`gamora-black-bolt-power-girl` Phase 1 + 2 closeout (2026-07-20 continuation 9):** opened the 9-phase work order `docs/work-orders/gamora-black-bolt-power-girl.md` against 13 verified findings (VF-20260720-001..013); closed Phases 1 (P0 persona isolation) and 2 (P0 CSP correction). Plan mandates: do **not** clear UI selection as a fix for persona leakage; do **not** broaden CSP to `https:/http:/file:/*`; do **not** expose filesystem paths or grant IDs to the model; do **not** trust renderer-supplied profile or grant selection. Resolution order: P0 persona → P0 CSP → P0 document agent → P1 folder menu → P1 prompt inspector → P1 character image → P1 media vault → docs / validation / QA.

- **Phase 1 — Persona isolation:** `src/utils/conversationKind.ts` (NEW) exports the `ConversationPersonaBinding` union plus `getConversationPersonaBinding(conversation)` which reads ONLY `conversation.metadata.character`. `src/stores/chat-stream-manager.ts resolveCharacterSlug` and `buildStreamBody` rewritten to consult only the binding; `useCharacterStore.getState().selectedCharacterSlug` global fallback is gone. `src/stores/chat-stream-manager.test.ts` (NEW, 7 PASS).
- **Phase 2 — CSP correction:** `electron/utils/rendererCsp.ts:39` widened to `'self' data: blob: venice-character-cache: venice-media:`. `media-src` left untouched. `electron/utils/rendererCsp.test.ts` (+11, 3 PASS).
- **Combined Phase 1+2 validation:** `npx vitest run --fileParallelism=false src/stores/chat-stream-manager.test.ts electron/utils/rendererCsp.test.ts` → **21/21 PASS in 1.53 s**. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json` → **0 errors**. `lint:eslint -- --quiet` → **0 warnings**.

**`gamora-black-bolt-power-girl` Phase 3 §3.7 closeout (2026-07-20 continuation 10 — bounded multi-turn agent loop):** audit-confirmed that `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.ts runChatAgentLoop` performed exactly one streaming turn + one tool batch and returned; the agent never iterated, never replied after seeing its own tool outputs, and never self-corrected. Fix extracts `streamAndExecuteTurn()` helper and wraps it in `MAX_AGENT_TURNS = 8`/`MAX_AGENT_TOOL_CALLS = 16` loop with explicit guard-block propagation and abort handling. Termination paths:
- `result.kind === "blocked"` → return immediately (canonical 451 shape preserved).
- `!turnResult.hasToolCalls` (model emitted text + `finish_reason: "stop"` or similar) → return final response.
- `request.signal?.aborted` between turns → exit cleanly.
- `MAX_AGENT_TOOL_CALLS` reached (16) or `MAX_AGENT_TURNS` reached (8) → exit cleanly with last streamed result.
- **Body rebuild on continuation:** `{ ...currentBody, messages: [...previousMessages, assistantMessage(tool_calls:[...]), ...toolResultMessages] }`. The model now sees its own tool outputs and decides whether more tool work or a final answer is appropriate.
- **`TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS = 50_000`** hoisted from inline literal. **Fallback VeniceIpcResponse** now fully-typed (`statusText`, `headers`, `contentType`).
- **Regression coverage:** `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.test.ts` (4 EXISTING cases re-routed through `installSingleTurnMock(emitFirstTurn)` helper); `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.multiturn.test.ts` (NEW, 5 cases / 5 PASS): two-turn happy path, `MAX_AGENT_TURNS=8` cap, body messages append integrity, abort between turns, guard-block propagation.
- **Combined Phase 3 §3.7 validation:** `npx vitest run electron/agent/runtime/` → **26/26 PASS in 1.65 s**. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json` → **0 errors**. `lint:eslint --max-warnings=0` → **0 warnings**.
- **Phase 3 remaining sub-steps** (§3.1 dedicated Component, §3.2 dedicated IPC channel, §3.3 grantId-from-model leak in `agent-tool-executor.ts`, §3.4 schema matrix, §3.5 unified `document.create`, §3.6 unimplemented-tool unadvertise, §3.10 `media.generateImage` executor contract hardening, §3.11 `DocumentAgentChat.tsx` UI, §3.12 17-bullet acceptance matrix) remain pending and progress to continuation 12.

**Dependency-audit status (refreshed 2026-07-26):** `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` reports 16 high-severity transitive `brace-expansion` findings in Electron packaging dependencies. npm offers only `npm audit fix --force`, which would install the breaking Electron Builder 25.1.8 downgrade. No forced downgrade or advisory suppression was applied; the aggregate `npm run ci` gate therefore remains blocked at the audit step while every later gate is independently validated.

### 2026-07-20 (continuation 10) — `gamora-black-bolt-power-girl` Phase 3 §3.7 closeout (bounded multi-turn agent loop)

- **Scope:** Opened Phase 3 §3.7 of `docs/work-orders/gamora-black-bolt-power-girl.md`. Audit-confirmed `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.ts runChatAgentLoop` performed exactly one streaming turn + one tool batch and returned. The agent never iterated; the model never saw its own tool outputs; the loop could not reply, self-correct, or chain multi-step work. Fix extracts `streamAndExecuteTurn()` helper and wraps it in a bounded `MAX_AGENT_TURNS = 8`/`MAX_AGENT_TOOL_CALLS = 16` loop, with explicit guard-block propagation, abort handling between turns, and a body rebuild on every continuation so the model sees the assistant tool_calls message + tool result messages it produced. Fallback when no result ever streams emits a fully-typed `VeniceIpcResponse` (no partial stub). The other 11 Phase 3 sub-steps (§3.1 dedicated Component, §3.2 dedicated IPC, §3.3 grantId-from-model leak, §3.4 schema matrix, §3.5 unified document.create, §3.6 unadvertise unimplemented tools, §3.10 media.generateImage contract hardening, §3.11 chat-agent UI, §3.12 17-bullet acceptance matrix) remain pending and progress to continuation 11.
- **Implementation (`electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.ts`):**  
  - Refactor: extracted `streamAndExecuteTurn(profileId, agentSessionId, body, signal, onDelta) → TurnResult` per-turn helper. Returns `{ result, finishReason, aggregatedToolCalls, appendedMessages: ToolResultMessage[], hasToolCalls }`.  
  - `runChatAgentLoop(request, onDelta)` now iterates `for (let turn = 0; turn < MAX_AGENT_TURNS; turn++)` and:
    - Returns the existing result on `result.kind === "blocked"` (canonical 451 shape preserved, no follow-up turn).
    - Returns the existing result on `!turnResult.hasToolCalls` (model emitted text + `finish_reason: "stop"` or similar — natural assistant stop).
    - Checks `request.signal?.aborted` before dispatching the next turn.
    - Tracks `totalToolCallCount += turnResult.aggregatedToolCalls.size` and exits when `totalToolCallCount >= MAX_AGENT_TOOL_CALLS`.
    - Rebuilds `currentBody.messages = [...previousMessages, assistantMessage(tool_calls:[…]), ...toolResultMessages]` before the next stream.
    - Falls back to a fully-typed `{ ok:false, status:500, statusText:"Internal Server Error", headers:{}, body:{error:"agent loop produced no response"}, contentType:"application/json" }` when no result ever streams (fixes the pre-existing `TS2322` on a shape-stripped stub).
  - Type tightening: `appendedMessages` is `ToolResultMessage[]` (`{role:"tool", tool_call_id, name, content, metadata?}`) — narrower than the historical `Record<string, unknown>[]` to satisfy the existing `SseChunk.appendedMessages` contract.
- **Test refactor:** `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.test.ts` (4 EXISTING cases) re-routed through `installSingleTurnMock(emitFirstTurn)` helper. First call invokes the test emitter (`tool_calls` + `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`); subsequent calls return a plain `finish_reason: "stop"` response so the bounded loop exits after the second dispatch without exhausting `MAX_AGENT_TURNS`. All 4 EXISTING cases still PASS.
- **New test file:** `electron/agent/runtime/chat-agent-runner.multiturn.test.ts` (NEW, 5 cases / 5 PASS):  
  1. Two-turn happy path (tool_calls → tool execution → final stop); second turn never dispatched after stop; appended tool messages count = 1.  
  2. `MAX_AGENT_TURNS = 8` cap: 8 sequential tool_calls responses → exactly 8 `performGuardedVeniceRequest` calls then stops.  
  3. Body messages append integrity: turn-1 body = `[user]`; turn-2 body = `[user, assistant(tool_calls:[workspace.list]), tool(tool_call_id:call_aa, content:…)]` — canonical OpenAI-style chat-completion conversation shape preserved.  
  4. Abort between turns respected: `controller.abort()` after turn 1 → 1 dispatch.  
  5. Guard-block propagation: `{kind:"blocked", block:{…451…}}` → 1 dispatch, immediate return.
- **Constraint compliance:** stayed on `main`, no commit / no push, no verifier-script edits, no `dist:mac` / `dist:win`, no `package.json` edits. No unrelated-file edits. No API keys exposed. No raw prompt text logged (loop body uses canonical `tool_call_id`/`content` messages; nothing leaks to parameters).

### 2026-07-20 — Phase 2.6 folder-backup encryption rewrite (libsodium)

- **Service body rewrite (`electron/services/chatFolderBackupService.ts`):** replaced the prior `crypto.randomBytes().toString("base64")`-as-passphrase pattern (which stored the random IV in the `keyWrapped` field) with a libsodium Argon2id13 + XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF envelope. Per backup: 256-bit fresh DEK (`crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_KEYBYTES`), 16-byte salt, Argon2id-derived KEK at `_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE` / `_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE`, KEK nonce, and an independent payload nonce. Wire format v2 ships `{ version: 2, exportedAt, kdf: { algorithm: "argon2id13", opslimit, memlimit }, crypto: { salt, kekNonce, wrappedKey, payloadNonce, ciphertext }, publicHeader: { sourceFolderKind, sourceFolderName, createdAt, appVersion, includesMedia, conversationCount } }`. The clear-text manifest never appears on disk; conversations, messages, and folder metadata live exclusively inside the encrypted payload while `publicHeader` carries only the labels needed for passwordless preview.
- **Crypto init fix (Vitest ESM timing):** at module load the constants `_sodium.crypto_pwhash_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE` / `_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE` were `null` because Vitest's ESM build path did not await `_sodium.ready`. Replaced the eager module-level `const ARGON2_OPSLIMIT = …` reads with a lazy `getArgonConstants()` helper that resolves an `_sodiumReadyPromise` once and caches the constants; `exportBackup` and `getActiveKdfParameters` await it before invoking `crypto_pwhash`. The import path was already correct because opslimit/memlimit travel with the envelope, so `_sodiumReadyPromise` threaded through the import call-path resolves the rest.
- **IPC validator hardening (`electron/ipc/handlers/chatFolderHandlers.ts`):** added `isExportFolderBackupInput()` (rejects empty / missing / sub-8-char passphrase and `passphraseConfirmed === false`) and `isImportFolderBackupInput()` (enforces passphrase ≥ 8 chars + mode + optional `targetFolderId`). Both `chat-folders:export-backup` and `chat-folders:import-backup` handlers run their validators before reaching the service so empty passphrases fail closed at the IPC boundary.
- **Structured-error preservation:** introduced a private `BackupStructureError extends Error` class so structural rejections (missing public header, unsupported version, malformed JSON envelope) propagate their descriptive `missing the encrypted public header` message while Argon2id / AEAD-tag failures still funnel to the canonical `Wrong passphrase or corrupt backup file` user message. `previewImport` reads only the publicHeader and no longer requires the `crypto` block, exactly matching the documented preview-without-passphrase contract.
- **Regression coverage (`electron/services/chatFolderBackupService.test.ts`, 8 new tests):**
  1. **Wire-format enforcement** envelope contains only `version / exportedAt / kdf / crypto / publicHeader`, never `keyWrapped` / `passphrase` / `metadata.ciphertext`, and the conversation body (`"messages":`) never appears in cleartext (the `sourceFolderName` in `publicHeader` is allowed by design).
  2. **Passphrase length gate** — service rejects empty / < 8-char passphrases.
  3. **`passphraseConfirmed: false` rejection** — service refuses to encrypt until the IPC layer confirms.
  4. **Locked-folder rejection** — locked folders cannot be exported; service returns `{ ok: false, error: /lock/i }`.
  5. **Empty passphrase on import** returns `{ ok: false, error: /passphrase/i }`.
  6. **Wrong passphrase** returns exactly `"Wrong passphrase or corrupt backup file"` (canonical user-facing string).
  7. **AEAD tag mismatch** (single-byte tampering of the ciphertext) also returns the same canonical message — never leaks the decrypted bytes even partially.
  8. **v1 legacy backup** (no `publicHeader`) rejected with the structured `BackupStructureError("Envelope is missing the encrypted public header")`.
- **Validation executed this session** (all run from `/Users/super_user/Projects/Venice_Forge`):
  - `npx vitest run electron/services/chatFolderBackupService.test.ts` → **8/8 passed**.
  - `npm run test:electron` → **724/724 passed across 67 files**.

### 2026-07-18 — Custom-protocol CORS regression guard (`VERIFY-155`)

- **Root cause:** Electron defaults `corsEnabled` to `false` for `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged`, so cross-origin `<video>`/`<audio>`/`<img>`/`fetch` from `http://localhost:5173` to `venice-media://…`, `venice-tts://…`, and `venice-character-cache://…` was rejected by Chromium with `net::ERR_FAILED` even though `stream: true` was set and the schemes appeared in `media-src`. Fixed by explicitly setting `corsEnabled: true` on all three schemes (keeping `stream: true` on the audio/video schemes) and adding a narrow main-process origin guard that emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` equal to the renderer origin (never `*`), `Vary: Origin`, and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Accept-Ranges, Content-Length, Content-Range, Content-Type` on every successful response.
- **Centralised helper:** added `electron/utils/customProtocolAccess.ts` exporting `evaluateCustomProtocolAccess`, `buildCorsHeaders`, `DEV_RENDERER_ORIGIN`, `EXPOSED_MEDIA_HEADERS`. Dev-mode renderer (`http://localhost:5173`) and the packaged `file://` renderer (validated against the canonical `rendererRoot` referrer and rejected when the referrer is missing or escapes the dir) are the only allowed origins.
- **Per-protocol hand-off:**
  - `electron/main.ts`: rewrote the `registerSchemesAsPrivileged([...])` block to carry `corsEnabled: true` on every renderer-consumed scheme and `stream: true` on the audio/video ones. Continues to resolve the identifier `GENERATED_MEDIA_SCHEME` from `electron/services/generatedMediaStore.ts`.
  - `electron/utils/characterImageCacheProtocol.ts`: collapsed into a 12-line façade that delegates to the shared helper. Replaced the empty `extends CustomProtocolAccessInput {}` interface with a `type` alias to satisfy `@typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type`.
  - `electron/services/generatedMediaStore.ts`: `createGeneratedMediaResponse(id, request, access)` now requires an `access: CustomProtocolAccessInput`, runs the guard before any byte is read or streamed, returns `403 { error: "Origin not permitted" }` on rejection, and emits the CORS headers via `buildCorsHeaders` without overwriting the byte-range headers.
- **Regression coverage:**
  - **Static audit** — `scripts/verify-custom-protocol-privileges.cjs` parses the `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` block in `electron/main.ts`, accepts either string-literal (`"venice-media"`) or identifier (`GENERATED_MEDIA_SCHEME`) registrations, and asserts that every renderer-consumed scheme has `secure/standard/supportFetchAPI/corsEnabled` and that the audio/video schemes additionally carry `stream: true`. New schemes trigger a violation that names the unknown protocol and recommends `corsEnabled: true`.
